checklist.evidence: query_database.py:686 assigns open_error unconditionally at the end of the `async with _conversation_turn(...)` body (line 610), after the agent-run try/except (632-680) whose every failure branch re-raises. _conversation_turn (177-208) yields on both the conversation_id None path (194-196) and the locked path, so the body always runs; unqueued calls still execute line 686 (only the rollback at 687 is gated on queued_id). checklist.claim: If components_to_blocks/trace assembly raises after the open_error rollback, the client gets _INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE instead of the memory-unavailable message, contradicting criterion 1 (check ordering).
checklist.evidence: src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:690-699: components_to_blocks failure raises RuntimeError(_INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE) before the open_error check at line 731, after the rollback at 688. So when open_error is set and formatting raises, the client gets the internal error, not the memory-unavailable message. The defect exists for components_to_blocks. Trace assembly (718-725) is caught and does not preempt, so the claim is only partly accurate.

Calls at :659-661 and :688 pass (agent, queued_id, baseline_user.id, baseline_messages): queued_id is str|None narrowed to str by the guard (_conversation_turn yields str|None, :178), User.id is str (agent/core/user/models.py:15), baseline_messages is int. baseline_messages is bound unconditionally at :612 (=0) before any branch, and every call is guarded by baseline_user is not None and queued_id is not None.

checklist.claim: The comment's claim that a memory-less turn's messages are removed before the next call on this conversation can build on them holds for every case (incl. no conversation_id, baseline_user or queued_id None).
checklist.source_excerpt:

checklist.evidence: The rollback at src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:683-688 runs only when send_message completes without raising and requires baseline_user and queued_id non-None. (1) conversation_id None: no rollback, but harmless because the agent mints a private id no caller can name (docstring lines 178-190), and baseline_user is None only when queued_id is None, so the guard adds no gap. (2) Counterexample: if send_message raises on a turn that ran with agent_memory.open_error set, the except Exception at ~641-646 only calls _trim_unanswered_tool_use (removes from the first unanswered tool_use, not the whole turn) and re-raises, so the open_error read/rollback at 686-688 is never reached; the turn's remaining messages stay in the conversation. (3) _rollback_conversation (374-460) swallows failures and returns without removing messages: store without truncate_messages, ConversationOwnerMismatchError, other exceptions (logged at ERROR), and truncate returning False (evicted). So the 'removed here, before the next call can build on it' claim is not true for every case.

checklist.claim: AC3: recovery without restart; first successful open returns normal results with memory_info hits/misses; a late failed open after a concurrent successful open causes no later error.
checklist.evidence: agent_memory.py:136-152 leaves _client None on failed open (records _open_error, re-raises) so the next call retries, and sets _open_error=None and _client on success: recovery without restart. open_error property (155-164) returns None whenever _client is not None, so a late failed open after a concurrent success cannot leave it set. query_database.py:686,731 raises the memory-unavailable error only when open_error is not None; otherwise 743-751 returns normal markdown/blocks/memory_info from components_to_blocks. Tests (test_memory_unavailable.py:82-101, 163-177) read consistent.

checklist.claim: AC4: when the memory object has no open_error attribute, query_database results are unchanged.
checklist.evidence: query_database.py:686 reads open_error via getattr(getattr(agent,'agent_memory',None),'open_error',None), so a missing attribute (or missing agent_memory) yields None. The rollback at 687-688 is gated on open_error is not None, and the raise at 731-742 is gated on open_error is not None. With None neither runs and flow continues to the unchanged is_error handling at 743.
